name: Healthcare Crisis Response Playbooks
description: Approved operational response actions for public-health surveillance alerts.

monitor.action: Check the latest reports for missing data, delays or an unusual increase
Ask the facilities reporting the largest increases to confirm their figures and current workload

investigate.action: Confirm the increase with the facilities and laboratories that supplied the data
Check staffing, test capacity and essential supply levels at the busiest facilities
Prepare a short internal update that states what increased, where it increased and what remains uncertain

escalate.action: Open an incident response call and assign named owners to the immediate actions
Start a daily report of new cases, laboratory results, facility pressure and data gaps
Move staff and essential supplies to the facilities reporting the greatest pressure
Prepare an approved public update with clear prevention advice and information on when to seek care

monitor.action: Compare today's fever, cough and breathing-illness visits with the previous four weeks and list the facilities reporting the largest increases
Confirm how many influenza and respiratory tests are positive, pending or delayed at reporting laboratories
Check reported stocks of masks, oxygen supplies, fever medicines and antiviral medicines at the busiest facilities

investigate.action: Ask the facilities reporting the largest increases to confirm respiratory visit counts, triage wait times, available isolation space and staff absences
Confirm respiratory test turnaround times, the number of samples waiting and any reporting delays
Count available masks, oxygen supplies, fever medicines and antiviral medicines at facilities with the highest respiratory demand
Prepare a one-page internal update covering respiratory visits, test results, facility pressure and unresolved data gaps

escalate.action: Activate respiratory surge plans at the busiest facilities, including separate respiratory triage and staffed isolation areas
Start daily reporting of respiratory visits, admissions, available isolation spaces and staff absences by facility
Prioritize respiratory samples from the most affected facilities and report the testing backlog each day
Move masks, oxygen supplies, fever medicines and antiviral medicines to facilities with the highest respiratory demand
Prepare an approved public message on respiratory symptoms, ways to reduce spread and where to seek care

monitor.action: Compare today's vomiting and diarrhea visits with the previous four weeks and list the facilities or shared settings reporting the largest increases
Confirm how many stool tests are positive, pending or delayed at reporting laboratories
Check oral rehydration solution, IV fluid and cleaning-supply levels at the busiest facilities

investigate.action: Ask the highest-reporting facilities whether patients share a school, care home, event, food source or water source
Confirm stool-test turnaround times, the number of samples waiting and any reporting delays
Count oral rehydration solution, IV fluids, disinfectant and protective equipment at facilities with the highest diarrhea demand
Prepare a one-page internal update covering illness reports, possible shared food or water sources, test results and data gaps

escalate.action: Coordinate inspection and sampling of the specific food, water or shared setting linked to the illness reports
Start daily reporting of vomiting and diarrhea visits, affected facilities, shared exposure links and test results
Prioritize stool and water samples linked to the affected locations and report the testing backlog each day
Move oral rehydration solution, IV fluids and cleaning supplies to facilities reporting the greatest demand
Prepare an approved public message on safe food and water, handwashing, symptoms and where to seek care

monitor.action: Check hospital grounds, drains and water containers for standing water; record any mosquito breeding sites for removal
Confirm how many dengue tests are positive, pending or delayed at reporting laboratories
Compare recent fever visits by locality and list the facilities reporting the largest increases

investigate.action: Ask the local mosquito-control team to inspect neighborhoods around the facilities reporting the largest increases and list standing-water sites
Check dengue test-kit stocks, IV fluid supplies and referral capacity at facilities serving the affected localities
Start a daily locality report of suspected dengue visits, positive tests, pending tests and reporting delays
Prepare an internal dengue update covering affected localities, standing-water reports, test results, facility readiness and data gaps

escalate.action: Start targeted inspections and removal of standing water and mosquito breeding sites in the most affected localities
Require daily facility reporting of suspected dengue visits, positive tests, pending tests and referral needs by locality
Move dengue test kits and IV fluid supplies to high-demand facilities and confirm referral capacity for patients with warning signs
Prepare an approved public message on removing standing water, preventing mosquito bites, dengue warning signs and where to seek care

ili: Check whether fever, cough and breathing-illness visits are rising at the same facilities
Confirm respiratory test delays and stocks of masks, oxygen supplies and key medicines
age: Check whether vomiting and diarrhea reports point to the same school, care home, event, food source or water source
Confirm stool-test capacity and stocks of rehydration and cleaning supplies
dengue: Compare recent rain with reports of standing water and mosquito breeding sites
Confirm dengue test kits, IV fluid supplies, referral capacity and mosquito-control team availability
